new_statements.quote: While Stevenson (1942/2009) had discovered some tonal minimal pairs in Tira, including the ones in (11), he did not go into much detail about the tone system. One page is dedicated to a discussion about possible tone or stress and its relationship to intonation, where he observes that “inherent tone plays little part in distinguishing words” (Stevenson 1942/2009, p. 17). He admits that the details would still need to be worked out, but tentatively concludes that “Tira is not a tone language in the fullest sense of the term” (Stevenson 1942/2009, p. 17).

new_statements.rule_in_words: No accessible source says where word stress falls. The modern primary descriptions (Kaldhol 2024; Kaldhol, Rose & Simmons 2025) treat Tira as a two-tone language (H, L; word-final H͡L contour; H-spreading across words) and say nothing about word stress. The only stress-related content is second-hand: Stevenson's 1942 grammar (published 2009) has one page (p. 17) on 'possible tone or stress and its relationship to intonation', doubting that Tira is a tone language 'in the fullest sense'; Watters 1993 (abstract only accessible) discusses 'the relationships between tone, length and loudness' in ch. 3. Neither of those pages could be opened.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any accessible source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; no stress rule is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Kaldhol 2024 and Kaldhol et al. 2025 describe the Kadar dialect (Kauda area) from one speaker (Himidan Hassen), elicited words and sentences; Watters 1993 is a single-speaker case study of the El Akdar dialect; Stevenson's material was collected c. 1942. The quoted passage is Kaldhol's summary of Stevenson, not a first-hand stress statement; treat the stress question as unresolved.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog tira1254 (ISO tic) is language-level with no dialect children. Sources differ in variety: Kaldhol 2024 and Kaldhol, Rose & Simmons 2025 describe the Kadar dialect (Kauda area; single speaker Himidan Hassen, born 1991 in Komo); Watters 1993 is a single-speaker study of the El Akdar dialect; Stevenson's grammar (ms. 1942-43, publ. 2009) reflects 1940s speech; Alaki 2017 covers 'Litiro of Tombore'. Not to be confused with Tirax (maee1241, Vanuatu) or Tiro/Tira names elsewhere.
